name: Cervical Spondylosis
definition: Age-related degenerative change of cervical discs, facet/uncovertebral joints and adjacent bone; imaging abnormalities are common and require clinical correlation.

typical: Radiculopathy or myelopathy may coexist if neural structures are compressed

redFlags.item: Progressive limb weakness, gait imbalance or falls suggests cord/root compromise
Major trauma, infection or malignancy features require alternate urgent pathway

core: Upper-limb motor, reflex and sensory exam
Gait/balance when neurological symptoms are present

investigations.principle: Imaging is guided by clinical context and red flags; degenerative findings alone do not prove the pain generator.
investigations.MRI: Use when neurological compromise or other clinically important soft-tissue/neural pathology is suspected.
investigations.radiographs: May demonstrate alignment, disc-height loss and osteophytes.

amber: Medication/procedural choices require individualized risk review; progressive neurological features merit specialist assessment.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Possible Greeva-shoola/Vata-related symptom overlap may be discussed only as a correlation, not a one-to-one classical equivalent.

patientEducation.summary: Age-related degenerative change of cervical discs, facet/uncovertebral joints and adjacent bone; imaging abnormalities are common and require clinical correlation.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for new/progressive major weakness, gait deterioration, bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle sensory loss, fever/systemic illness with severe spinal pain, or cancer-associated neurological symptoms.

sources.title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Cervical Pain or Cervical Radiculopathy — Revised 2024
